It throws DomainError when those checks fail. The stock rules themselves sit on the Product entity (product.reserve and product.release), and the service coordinates them. It uses ProductRepository, which is an interface defined in the domain layer (src/domain/repositories.ts). Calling findById and save through a domain-owned interface is normal for a domain service. It is not persistence logic, because the file has no storage, query or serialization details. The file also has no transport, framework, or application-level work such as transactions, DTO mapping or authorization. The doc comment mentions an "in-memory catalogue", which hints at the storage technology, but it is only a comment and no code depends on it. There is some room for debate: calling save could be seen as application-layer orchestration, which is why confidence is not higher. Still, using a repository through a domain interface is acceptable in a domain service.
